name: arcs-sectors
title: Progress ring and pie
summary: A stroked 270° progress ring filled to 70%, and a three-slice pie whose slices meet exactly.
prompt: A circular progress ring at 70% with the percentage in the middle, next to a three-slice pie chart.
teaches: Draw a progress ring as two stroked arcs: a full 270° track and a partial value arc
Round the ends of an arc with strokeCap round
Build a pie from drawSector slices whose start angles continue each other
Switch the paint back to style fill before drawing text over stroked shapes
Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre

snippets.note: a 14 dp stroke with round caps for the ring
style fill again before the label, or the text is stroked 14 dp wide
a pie slice: drawSector from -90° (12 o'clock), 40% = 144°

check.describe: A blue ring three-quarters round and 70% filled; red, yellow and green slices meeting exactly. Resized, the whole drawing scales uniformly to fit and stays centred (smaller in a narrow box, centred with margins in a wide one).

pitfalls: Angles are in degrees, clockwise, with 0° at 3 o'clock: 12 o'clock is -90 and a gauge that opens at the bottom starts at 135
drawArc is only the curve: stroke it for a ring. With style fill it fills the chord between its ends; drawSector is the filled wedge that reaches the centre
Paint state persists: text drawn after the ring paint inherits style stroke and strokeWidth 14 and renders as an unreadable blob; set style fill first
Each slice's startAngle must equal the previous start + sweep, and the sweeps must add up to 360, or the pie shows gaps or overlaps

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: literal coordinates sit in the top-left and get cut off when it is resized, so scale the drawing to fit (or derive positions from componentWidth()/componentHeight())
